transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… my body’s been feeling like it’s not really listening to me. Like, at first I was pacing around my apartment all night, just going back and forth making these notes for a supper-club idea—actually the menu was kind of good, I had this whole thing with small plates—but anyway, I couldn’t stop moving.

And now it’s sort of the opposite. I’m so slowed down lately that my sister says I take forever just to get my shoes on. That’s mostly why I came in.
How long have you been feeling slowed down?

Um… the slowed-down part? It’s been, I’d say, about three months now. It kind of crept in and then just stayed, like everything got heavy. I remember thinking it was just a bad week, and then somehow it was a whole month, and then—yeah, around three months.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely energetic or irritable and didn't need much sleep?

Yeah… after I got fired, actually. Which was ridiculous, because the manager acted like I was the problem when the whole place was chaos—like they couldn’t even keep the patio section staffed right.

But after that, I felt weirdly… unstoppable? Like excited, like I was finally free to do all these big plans. And if anyone questioned me or told me to slow down, I’d just explode. Like my sister would say, “Maybe think this through,” and I’d feel like she was trying to ruin my entire life. It wasn’t just annoyed, it was like I couldn’t tolerate anyone getting in my way.
Have you ever felt really down or hopeless for a long time?

I mean… I don’t know if I’d call it hopeless exactly. “Down” is such a broad word, you know? Like sometimes I feel flattened out, but then I also get distracted thinking maybe it’s just because my apartment is a mess, and when the dishes pile up it makes everything feel worse. My sister says I over-explain that kind of thing.

So… yeah, I’m not sure how to answer that. I’ve felt off, definitely, but “really down or hopeless for a long time” — I don’t know.
When you're feeling really energetic, do you also feel really happy or on top of the world?

Yeah, kind of. After I got fired, I felt… not just happy, exactly, but like I was finally above all the stupid stuff, like nothing could stop me. I had all these plans and it felt exciting, like I’d figured something out.

But it could flip really fast. If someone questioned me or told me to slow down, I’d blow up, like they were trying to ruin my whole life. My sister did that a couple times and I just—yeah, I took it really personally.
Have you ever felt really down or hopeless for more than two weeks at a time?

Yeah… I think so. I keep trying to figure out when it started because time gets weird, like one week blends into the next, and then I’ll remember something random like when my neighbor’s dog kept barking for three nights and I was just lying there thinking the walls were too thin—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

But yeah, the heavy, slowed-down feeling has been there for… about three months now, I’d say. More than two weeks, definitely.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see?

I don’t think so. I mean, sometimes I’ll think I hear my phone or someone saying my name, but then it’s just the TV in the next apartment or like… the fridge making that weird noise. My apartment has terrible wiring too, so things hum.

But voices, like actual voices other people can’t hear, or seeing things… no, I haven’t really noticed anything like that.
Did you ever hear voices or see things that weren't there when you were feeling really energetic or unstoppable?

I don’t think so… not like voices talking to me or seeing actual people or things that weren’t there. When I was in that “unstoppable” mode, everything felt intense, and I’d get caught up in little signs or coincidences, like a song coming on at the exact right time—actually, there was this one night at the diner where the lights kept flickering and I thought it meant something, but the wiring there is awful, so…

But hearing voices or seeing stuff, no, I can’t say that happened.
When you're feeling really energetic, does it feel like a completely different state from when you're feeling slowed down?

Yeah, it’s… it’s not just like being in a better mood. It feels like my whole body switches gears. Like for a while I had this nonstop energy where I couldn’t even sit through a meal, or watch a soccer game, without jumping up to do something.

I’d be making calls, sketching menu ideas on napkins, reorganizing the kitchen—actually the kitchen at work drives me crazy because nobody puts the prep containers back right, and then you lose ten minutes looking for lids—but yeah, it’s completely different from when I’m slowed down. In that state I can’t stay still.
Do you ever find yourself quickly switching between feeling energetic and feeling slowed down?

Yeah… that’s kind of the whole reason I came in, honestly. It’s like my body won’t pick one speed. At first I was pacing around my apartment all night, making notes for this supper-club idea—like menus, seating, who would bring what, and then I’d remember I need to text somebody about plates or whatever.

And now lately it’s the opposite. I feel so slowed down it’s embarrassing. My sister said the other day it takes me forever just to get my shoes on, and she wasn’t wrong. I’ll just be sitting there with one shoe in my hand like I forgot what the next step is. So yeah, it switches, and it feels really out of my control.
Did you ever lose touch with reality when you were feeling extremely energetic or unstoppable?

I’m not totally sure what counts as “losing touch,” honestly. Like, I felt really sure of myself—too sure, probably—and I’d get wrapped up in ideas, but I don’t know that I was, like, not in reality.

I mean, I was still going to work and talking to people, though I was all over the place. At the restaurant, when it’s busy, you kind of have to track like six tables and remember who needs ranch and who said no onions—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

So… I don’t think I lost touch with reality in the way you mean, but I might need you to explain what that would look like.
When you were feeling extremely energetic or unstoppable, did you ever believe things that weren't true, like thinking you had special powers or that people were out to get you?

I don’t think I believed I had special powers or anything like that. Like, I wasn’t thinking I could fly or read minds or… whatever. And I don’t remember thinking people were out to get me.

I mean, I did get really convinced my ideas were good, like way more convinced than usual, and I’d talk about them like they were obviously going to work. But that’s different, right? Like when you’re at work and you know a table’s going to complain before they even say anything—sorry, that’s not the same thing.

So… no, not like special powers or paranoia, at least not that I noticed.
When you're feeling extremely energetic, is that a normal part of who you are, or does it feel abnormal to you?

It doesn’t feel normal to me. Like, after I got fired, instead of being crushed the way I probably should’ve been, I felt… weirdly excited? Like I was unstoppable, like maybe this was actually the best thing that could’ve happened because now I could finally do all these plans I had.

But then if anyone questioned it—my sister especially, or anybody saying, “Maybe slow down”—I’d just snap. Like, really blow up, like they were trying to ruin my whole life or sabotage me. Which… I know sounds dramatic. I mean, people give advice all the time, like at work everybody has opinions about how you carry trays or stack glasses, and usually I can ignore it. But then I couldn’t. It felt abnormal, yeah.
When you're not feeling extremely energetic or slowed down, do you generally feel like you're able to control your emotions and reactions to things?

I think… mostly? Like when I’m just regular—not super up or super slowed down—I can usually keep a lid on things. I might get annoyed, but I don’t usually explode or anything.

Although, I guess it depends what you mean by “control.” Like at the restaurant, if a customer is rude, I can still smile and do the whole “I’ll check on that for you” thing, even if inside I’m like, are you kidding me. But then outside of work it’s different because you don’t have to pretend as much, you know?

So… yeah, generally I think I’m able to control my reactions when I’m not in one of those extremes. I haven’t really noticed a big problem then.
When you're feeling extremely energetic, does it feel like you're being yourself or more like someone else?

It feels like me, but turned way up, if that makes sense. Like after I got fired, I didn’t feel sad the way I expected—I felt weirdly excited, like I could do anything and all these plans were suddenly obvious.

But then if someone questioned me or said to slow down, I’d just… blow up. Like they were trying to ruin everything for me. And normally I’m not like that, not to that level. I can get annoyed, sure, like anybody, especially at work when people are being impossible, but this was different. So I guess it felt like me, but also not really me. More like some louder, angrier version of me.
When you're feeling extremely energetic, do you think your friends or family would say that's just you being you, or would they see it as a different side of you?

They’d probably say it’s a different side of me. I mean, at first maybe they’d think I was just being motivated or whatever, because I do get ideas and I talk a lot sometimes, but after I got fired I was… I don’t know, weirdly excited, like it was a good thing and I was unstoppable.

And my family, especially my sister, she wasn’t buying it. She’d say, “Slow down,” and I’d just blow up at her like she was trying to wreck my whole life. Which is not really how I usually am. I mean, we argue like any family, and she can be annoying about stuff—like she always has to comment on how I spend money or how late I sleep—but this was bigger than that. So yeah, I think they’d see it as not just me being me.
When you're feeling extremely energetic, do you think you're making decisions that are in line with your typical values and goals?

At the time, yeah, I thought they were. Like I really believed I was finally doing what I was supposed to be doing.

I had this whole idea that I was going to build the best bilingual supper club in the city—like food, music, Spanish and English, the whole thing—and I honestly thought investors would be dumb not to back me. Which sounds kind of ridiculous now because I didn’t even have a job then, and I definitely didn’t have the money lined up.

But in my head it felt completely reasonable. Like, I wasn’t thinking, “Is this practical?” I was thinking, “This is obviously going to work, why is everyone not seeing it?”
When you're feeling extremely energetic, do you think you're acting more impulsively than you usually do?

I’m not sure. I mean, I know people probably thought that, but in the moment it didn’t feel like “impulsive,” it felt like I was just moving fast because things finally made sense.

Like, I don’t know where the line is, you know? Because even at the restaurant, sometimes you have to make quick decisions—somebody complains about the food, the kitchen’s backed up, a table wants to leave, and you just handle it. So I’m used to kind of reacting fast. But this was… I don’t know. Maybe faster than usual? I’d have to think about it.
Do you find that your extremely energetic periods tend to happen at specific times or follow a certain pattern?

I don’t know if it’s like a pattern, exactly. It’s more like… it started after I got fired from the restaurant, and it’s been going on since then, maybe about four months now.

Which is weird, because restaurants always have drama—people quit, managers act like they own your whole life, customers get mad over nothing—so at first I thought maybe I was just reacting to that whole mess. But no, I guess if I’m being honest, it kind of tracks back to when I lost that job, and it hasn’t really let up since.
Have you ever had a period where you felt sad or empty for most of the day?

I don’t know… sad or empty like that? I mean, I’ve had bad days, sure. Everybody has. Like when you get home and the apartment is too quiet, or you realize you forgot to buy groceries and it’s just hot sauce and tortillas in the fridge—sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

Most of the day, though? I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve been tracking it that way. What do you mean by “empty,” exactly?

But no, I guess if I’m being honest, it kind of tracks back to when I lost that job, and it hasn’t really let up since.
